newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Cricket-Danny Morrison pulls out of Pakistan tour.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Danny Morrison pulls out of Pakistan tour.

text.p: SAHIWAL, Pakistan, Nov 18 (reuter) - New Zealand test hopes suffered a blow on Monday when their main strike bowler Danny Morrison pulled out of the Pakistan tour because of a groin problem.
Morrison had bowled just eight overs on the second day of the touring side's three-day game against a Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) XI on Monday.
The 30-year-old Auckland paceman, who has played 47 tests, had suffered the groin injury last week in Sharjah where he had to miss the Singer Trophy final against Pakistan.

"He complained about pain during his delivery stride and after the team's physio had examined him, it was decided not to risk the player in the two-test series against Pakistan," a team spokesman said.
Morrison will be flying home in a couple of days to recover for the test series against England in the new year.
He has been replaced by Otago paceman Robert Kennedy, who has played four tests. The 24-year-old bowler is expected to join his colleagues by the weekend.
The tourists ended the second day at 34 for one in their second innings after the local side had gained a lead of 22 runs.
Replying to the visitors' modest total of 171, the PCB XI began at 32 for two and declared the innings closed at tea with the total at 193 for seven.
Skipper Aqib Javed made a lusty unbeaten 23 with five fours in 38 balls, taking the score past New Zealand's total before returning to remove opener Craig Spearman in his second over.
At the close the two not out batsmen were Justin Vaughan on 20 and Bryan Young 12.
Middle order batsman Mahmood Hamid was the top scorer for the PCB XI, making a fine 39 from 82 balls with a six and four fours.
Opener Zahoor Elahi, 22 overnight, made 34 with seven fours from 43 balls, and his partner Sohail Jaffar took his score from three to 30.
Ahmer Saeed, Pakistan's under-19 player, contributed a useful 33 while Majid Inayat remained 19 not out when the innings was closed.
For New Zealand, paceman Simon Doull finished with two for 45 and left-arm spinner Mathhew Hart two for 58. Morrison did not add to the two wickets he picked up on Sunday.
